analysis.session_summary: Broad USD bid and risk-on tone dominated the Friday-close-to-Asia tape; DXY added 0.081% to 101.716 while VIX fell 3.903% to 19.084. USD/JPY led with +47.7 pips to 157.414 and JPY was the weakest major; EUR/USD was nearly flat at -2.2 pips. The only medium-confidence catalyst was the WSJ report that Trump was expected to remove some Canada tariffs, which briefly sent USD/CAD down -11.6 pips before a full retrace. Almost all other legs carried 'no clear catalyst' notes, leaving the tape vulnerable to the next headline.

themes.theme: Broad USD bid with no macro driver
themes.evidence: USD strength rank 1 (+0.112%), DXY +0.081%, USD/JPY +0.304%; most USD legs had no clear catalyst.
JPY strength -0.192 rank 8; VIX -3.903% to 19.084; USD/JPY +47.7 pips; CHF/JPY +22.2 pips.

themes.theme: Canada tariff relief briefly lifts CAD
themes.evidence: USD/CAD first leg down -11.6 pips on Trump tariff-removal headline with medium confidence; final USD/CAD +6.5 pips.

currency_drivers.USD: Broad dollar bid with no clear catalyst; DXY +0.081% and strength rank 1, selling rejected.
currency_drivers.EUR: Held its range, supported by France Moody's headlines; no major catalyst.
currency_drivers.JPY: Weakest major with no clear catalyst; attempt rejected, gave back 88%.
currency_drivers.GBP: Selling rejected, recovered 72%; no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.AUD: Selling rejected, recovered 66%; no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CAD: Closed at its best; tariff-removal headline briefly supported, rank 3.
currency_drivers.CHF: Attempt rejected, gave back 98%; no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.NZD: Selling rejected, recovered 74% but closed lower; no clear catalyst.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped in a 52.7-pip range, closing at 1.11911 (-2.2 pips); the largest down-leg from 03:30 to 14:45 (-51.5 pips) and the subsequent up-leg both lacked clear catalysts.

scenarios.name: Broad USD drift persists
scenarios.thesis: No first-tier catalyst before CB Consumer Confidence; the broad USD bid and VIX decline keep USD supported and JPY pressured.
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY breaks below 157.414 or VIX jumps above 19.084.

pair_paths.rationale: Repeat of the 22:00-00:00 down-leg; USD strength rank 1, EUR/USD closed -2.2 pips.
JPY weakest; first up-leg was +24.3 pips within a 98.9-pip range.
GBP/USD closed -12.8 pips; broad USD bid extends.

scenarios.name: Risk-on carry extends JPY weakness
scenarios.thesis: VIX fall (-3.903% to 19.084) and Canada tariff relief support carry; JPY stays weakest while AUD and CAD recover.
scenarios.invalidation: USD/CAD breaks above 1.40123 or VIX jumps above 19.084.

pair_paths.rationale: Largest USD/JPY up-leg was +74.2 pips; risk-on amplifies yen selling.
AUD/USD had a +16.0-pip up-leg from 07:00 to 10:30; selling rejected.
Initial tariff-relief headline produced a -11.6-pip USD/CAD down-leg.

scenarios.name: US data miss drives reversal
scenarios.thesis: CB Consumer Confidence (forecast 81.2 vs prior 81.9) disappoints, unwinding the broad USD bid and lifting EUR/USD.
scenarios.invalidation: DXY closes above 101.716 and USD/JPY above 157.414.

pair_paths.rationale: First EUR/USD up-leg was +28.2 pips; reversal would challenge range highs.
USD/JPY had a -47.2-pip down-leg from 01:15 to 03:30; risk off unwinds.
Initial USD/CHF down-leg was -16.9 pips; CHF attempt rejected reversal.

risks.why_it_matters: Most legs had confidence 'none'; no macro anchor.
Only scheduled medium-impact USD release; forecast 81.2 vs prior 81.9.
USD/CAD initially fell -11.6 pips on tariff relief, then closed +6.5 pips; CAD strength rank 3 could fade.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: CB Consumer Confidence is the next scheduled USD release (forecast 81.2 vs prior 81.9); a miss could extend the USD selling rejection seen early in the window.
